notes.1: Question 1 was answered correctly by 31 per cent of the candidates who chose option A . 24 per cent chose option B , 41 per cent chose option C and 4 per cent chose option D . The term capital in economics is used to describe a non-financial asset or factor of production, which may be used to produce other goods. It is not the money used to finance a project (option C ).
notes.9: Question 9 was answered correctly by 35 per cent of the candidates who chose option B . 33 per cent chose option A , 17 per cent chose option C and 15 per cent chose option D . If there was an increase in the number of workers unemployed then the potential supply of labour is likely to have increased and this would weaken the bargaining strength of a trade union representing existing workers (option B ).
notes.17: Question 17 was answered correctly by 32 per cent of the candidates who chose option B . 23 per cent chose option A , 19 per cent chose option C and 26 per cent chose option D . Option B is the only option that both describes a fiscal policy and a change in supply.
notes.23: Question 23 was answered correctly by 38 per cent of the candidates who chose option D . 26 per cent chose option A , 18 per cent chose option B and 19 per cent chose option C . When an indicator rises at a slower rate than in previous years, it is still an increase in the variable being measured. It has increased, but not as fast as it increased in previous years. Thus, in 2013 prices still rose, by 3 per cent. They did not rise as fast as in 2012, when they rose by 5 per cent.
